title: Pollyanna and Polynomially \c{hi}-Bounded Graph Classes
summary: A hereditary graph class is called polynomially $χ$-bounded if there exists a polynomial function $f$ such that $χ(G) \le f(ω(G))$ for every induced subgraph $G$. A class $\mathcal{C}$ is called Pollyanna if, for every $χ$-bounded class $\mathcal{F}$, the class $\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}$ is polynomially $χ$-bounded. In the paper by Chudnovsky et al., \emph{Reuniting $χ$-boundedness with polynomial $χ$-boundedness} (J.\ Combin.\ Theory Ser.\ B 176 (2026), 30--73), the authors posed twelve problems and one conjecture concerning the Pollyanna framework.
